incident: Norsk Hydro - LockerGoga ransomware (detected night of 18-19 March 2019)

sources.title: Microsoft (DART case study): Hackers hit Norsk Hydro with ransomware. The company responded with transparency
sources.what_it_gave: entry point (Dec 2018 email attachment from trusted customer, Trojan); first alert (antivirus days later); hops (standard user accounts -> admin credentials -> manual push of ransomware from Hydro's own domain controllers); detection (4 a.m. call 'We may be under attack', production stopped at some of 170 plants, network/servers shut down); impact (35,000 employees, 40 countries, thousands of servers and PCs, cost approaching USD 71 million); DART at Hungary plant

sources.title: BankInfoSecurity: Hydro Hit by LockerGoga Ransomware via Active Directory (NorCERT statement)
sources.what_it_gave: NorCERT: 'The attack was combined with an attack on Active Directory (AD)'; began Monday night at a U.S. plant and spread; plants in Norway, Qatar, Brazil run manually; Kripos informed Tuesday morning

sources.title: Hydro.com company history: 2019 cyber attack on Hydro
sources.what_it_gave: Extruded Solutions suffered most; Bauxite & Alumina, Primary Metal, Rolled Products, Energy kept producing via manual procedures; all PCs and servers reviewed/cleaned, encrypted machines rebuilt from backups

sources.title: Business Insurance / Reuters (30 Apr 2019): Hydro expects cyberattack costs of nearly $52 million in Q1
sources.what_it_gave: Q1 2019 cost estimate up to NOK 450 million (~USD 52m); Extruded Solutions external sales 333,000 t vs 362,000 t; production halted 19 March, other units manual; Q1 report postponed to 5 June

sources.title: SecurityWeek (5 Jun 2019): Ransomware Attack Costs Norsk Hydro Tens of Millions of Dollars (Q1 2019 report)
sources.what_it_gave: Q1 report: cost USD 35-41m in Q1 (NOK 300-350m first week), Q2 forecast NOK 200-250m; infection began 18 March; Extruded Solutions biggest impact; backups, no ransom paid

sources.title: Industrial Cyber: The Norsk Hydro Attack
sources.what_it_gave: detection 18-19 March overnight, warning signs morning of 19 March; alumina/bauxite kept on manual control; primary metal and rolled products harder to switch to manual; aluminium production never halted (electrolysis hardening risk); ~3 weeks to near-normal production
